A member noted timing of matching MSBA money must be planned for school building projects.
Members discussed whether an impervious surface fee or another source should fund drainage, and that no dedicated fund exists for culverts and bridges.
The gap between funds projected for capital and the five-year requests was described as large.
Funding was received for the Turkey Hill assessment and design work, which adds to department workload.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee, down to four members with a vacancy, nominated a new chair and vice chair; the recording does not capture the results.
A clerk was also to be appointed, but that vote is not audible in the captions, so no outcome can be stated.
Members discussed running a five-year capital plan alongside the next budget cycle, including templates, scoring, funding sources, stormwater and school building timing.
The chair is to bring a proposed plan on standardized information and data collection to the next meeting, working from the town manager's draft budget calendar.
The next meeting was set for Monday, July 29, at 7 p.m.; no budget votes were taken.

why_it_matters: The committee reviews the town's capital requests, so how it scores projects and sorts funding sources shapes which buildings, drainage and school projects reach a Town Meeting vote.
Residents raised small projects funded from leftover ARPA money and a possible override within two years; neither was decided, and the committee has not yet set its process.
